sentences.text: 1 2. The Applicant shall file legible and clearer copies of exempted documents, compliant with practice rules, before the next date of hearing.
3. Accordingly, the applications stand disposed of.
W.P.(C) 4376/2026 & CM APPL. 21265/2026 (for interim directions)
4. Mr. N.S. Vashisht, counsel for the Petitioners in the above petitions, submits that the limited prayer before this Court is for rectification of the revenue records.
He states that the subject lands were mutated in the name of 'Sarkar Daulat Madar' pursuant to acquisition proceedings initiated by the Government of NCT of Delhi for the Delhi Development Authority.
1 The said acquisition proceedings were, however, quashed, and such quashing has been upheld up to the Supreme Court.

While dismissing the appeals vide order dated 31st August, 2016, the Supreme Court granted liberty to DDA to initiate fresh acquisition proceedings within a period of one year by issuing a notification under Section 11 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It was further observed that, in the event no such proceedings were initiated within the said period and DDA was in possession, the physical possession of the land shall be returned to the original landowners.
5. Mr. Vashisht submits that, in both cases, physical possession of the subject land is presently with the Petitioners.
He further contends that, despite the liberty granted by the Supreme Court to initiate fresh acquisition proceedings within one year, no such steps have been taken for the past ten "DDA"
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

Notwithstanding the above, the revenue records continue to reflect the land as mutated in the name of the Government.
The Petitioners' limited grievance, therefore, is that such mutation entries, which no longer reflect the factual position, are liable to be rectified.
6. On this short issue, Ms. Shobhana Takiar, Standing Counsel for the DDA, accepts notice and states that she will take instructions.

7. Re-notify on 18th May, 2026.
SANJEEV NARULA, J APRIL 6, 2026/ab
